portInfo.description: Portsmouth International Port is Britain’s largest municipal port (Portsmouth City Council) and a ferry, freight and cruise gateway on the Solent. Cruise operations use dedicated passenger facilities at the port’s extended berth, ceremonially named the Ayrton Berth after Hertha Ayrton. The port’s cruise-trade pages position Portsmouth for boutique/mid-size turnarounds and calls, with a complimentary water shuttle to the waterfront for calling ships when operated. Confirm berth assignment and shuttle on the day — do not assume walk-off into Gunwharf Quays from the cruise berth without the shuttle or a taxi.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Historic Dockyard / HMS Victory area (waterfront) — ~120 min; tickets/hours not verified here.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Portsmouth homepage notes that EU EES checks happen at destination ports, not at Portsmouth International Port, for ferry travellers — still irrelevant to UK arrival rules for cruise passengers entering the UK here.
